topic: What if Ace ignored Akainu's taunt at Marineford and survived
title: What If Ace Survived Marineford?
description:
What if Ace ignored Akainu's taunt in chapter 573 and kept running? Whitebeard still falls, Blackbeard still takes the Gura Gura no Mi, but Luffy, Sabo and the Mera Mera no Mi all take a very different road. Follow the cause and effect, one consequence at a time.

Chapters: see below. Would you trade Ace's death for Sabo's reunion with Luffy? Tell me in the comments.
comment: Would you save Ace if it meant Sabo never meets Luffy at Dressrosa, or is the story better as it is? Pick one.

lines.text: What if Ace ignored Akainu's insult at Marineford and kept running?

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: What if the greatest tragedy in One Piece simply never happened?

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: How different would Luffy become? And who pays the price for Ace being alive?

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: To understand how everything changes, we have to go back to the Summit War of Marineford.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace is about to be executed in front of the entire world, and his crew has sailed into the Marine headquarters to stop it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Edward Newgate, Whitebeard, the strongest man alive, leads the largest pirate army ever gathered.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And Luffy, Ace's little brother, has broken out of Impel Down just to be there.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In the real story, the plan works. Ace is freed.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Then Akainu opens his mouth, and the war turns into a funeral.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Hold on to that moment, because it is the only thing we are changing.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Chapter 573. Ace is running toward the ships with Luffy at his side.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Whitebeard has just given his final captain's order: every man must live and return to the New World.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Admiral Sakazuki, Akainu, watches them go and decides to say one thing.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He calls Whitebeard a failure, a man who never beat Roger and never became Pirate King.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon, Ace stops. He turns around. And that is where it ends for him.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: People call it a mistake, and honestly, I understand why. Ace was defending the man who gave him a family.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But here is the part people forget. Akainu didn't win a fight. He won an argument with Ace's pride.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So in this version, Ace does something he rarely does. He keeps his temper and keeps running.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He doesn't forgive the insult. He just remembers that Whitebeard's last order was to live.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Akainu shouts after him, but magma can't catch a man who won't turn around.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace and Luffy reach the sea. The Whitebeard Pirates begin their retreat.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And for the first time in the war, the Marines are losing their prize.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Think about what Ace carries into that moment: a bounty of 550 million berries and a Pirate King's blood he never asked for.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He has spent his whole life asking if he deserves to be alive. Running from the insult is a harder choice than fighting it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now, the first ripple. Whitebeard.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Whitebeard is already dying. The Marines hit him, his own subordinate Squard stabbed him, and his body is spent.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon he holds the line so his sons can escape. That doesn't change, because it was never about Ace alone.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He stays on the battlefield, laughing, shaking the world, buying every second his crew needs.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: The difference is what he sees while he does it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He sees Ace alive, on a ship, sailing away.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In the real story, Whitebeard dies on his feet, and then declares that the One Piece exists.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In this one, he still dies. Oda wouldn't let a legend leave quietly any other way.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But his last words are the same, and this time the son who matters most is alive to hear about them.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now, here's the part that changes everything.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Blackbeard. Marshall D. Teach.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Remember why Ace was captured in the first place. He chased Teach for killing Thatch, a fellow commander.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace lost that fight, and Teach handed him to the Marines like a trade.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon, Blackbeard walks into Marineford, takes Whitebeard's Gura Gura no Mi, and nobody can stop him.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Chapter 577. A black cloth, a dead man, and a second Devil Fruit in one body.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That still happens here. Ace being alive doesn't stop the one thing that Teach planned for years.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But now there is a living witness who knows exactly what he did.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And Ace is not Luffy. He doesn't forget a score. He has a murdered friend and a stolen fruit to settle.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Here's my read: Ace goes after Blackbeard again, and this time he isn't alone.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But think about the problem he'd face. His Mera Mera no Mi is fire, and Blackbeard's Yami Yami no Mi swallows Logia powers.

shot.search: Mera Mera no Mi Yami Yami no Mi
shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace can't just burn Teach down. He needs a different answer.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: There's one more reason that decision matters. It tests whether Ace trusts the family he chose over the pride he was born with.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And honestly, that is the Ace I want to see: a man who finally picks living over being right.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now we come to Luffy, and this is where the story really breaks.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon, Luffy watches Ace die in his arms. His mind shuts down and Law has to operate to keep him alive.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He wakes on Amazon Lily and wants to give up. He nearly loses the will to live.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: It takes Jinbe, and later Rayleigh, to pull him out of it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In this version, none of that happens. Luffy still takes a beating at Marineford, but he walks away.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He is exhausted, bandaged, and scared, but he is not broken.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And that matters, because the Sabaody scattering still happens. Kuma still sends the crew apart.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So Luffy still loses his friends. He is still the captain who couldn't protect them.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But now his brother is the one who sits with him, not an empty seat.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: People say Ace's death is what made Luffy stronger. The steelman is that grief forged him.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But I'd push back. In canon, Luffy swore he would never lose anyone again. The crew's disappearance already gave him that vow.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So Luffy still trains with Rayleigh for two years. That part is protected by the story's own logic.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: What changes is the weight he carries into the New World.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: A Luffy who isn't carrying a grave is a freer Luffy. That is great news and a hidden problem.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now, the ripple nobody expects. Sabo.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Sabo lost his memory after the Celestial Dragon attack on his ship. He lived for years without knowing he had brothers.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: What brought it back? A newspaper. The headline that Ace and Whitebeard had died at Marineford.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He screamed, remembered the sake cups, remembered Luffy, and collapsed for days.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That is the whole trigger. Ace's death is the key that opens Sabo's memory.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Take it away, and the memory doesn't return that week. Maybe not for years.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And Sabo has another connection to Ace. The Mera Mera no Mi.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon, when Ace dies, his fruit is reborn as a new one, and ends up as the prize of the Dressrosa colosseum.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Sabo enters in disguise, and meets Luffy again after all those years.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Luffy lets him eat the fruit without a second thought, because it was Ace's.

shot.search: Sabo eats Mera Mera no Mi
shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But if Ace is alive, the fruit stays with Ace. There is no prize. There is no reason for Sabo to enter.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So the Dressrosa reunion never happens the way we saw it. Luffy and Sabo stay apart.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Two surviving brothers, one lost in memory, one always looking for him.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: It sounds like a gift for Ace, but it quietly costs Luffy the brother he thought he'd lost forever.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Quick reminder before we move on. Everything so far follows one rule: Ace changes one decision, and the world answers.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: No new powers appear, and nobody gets a convenient rescue. The war still costs Whitebeard his life.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now the other side of the war. The Marines.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Akainu pursues Ace, is blocked by Whitebeard's men, and comes away with a victory he doesn't enjoy.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In canon, he becomes Fleet Admiral. Sengoku resigns and Aokiji, Kuzan, walks away.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: The reason Kuzan left was Akainu's absolute justice. It was a pattern, not just one battle.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That doesn't change. Even without the kill, the war ends with the Marines' pride cracked.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: But here's something fans miss. Ace's death was the Marines' real victory.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Without it, the world government loses its proof that the Roger bloodline is gone.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace is the son of the Pirate King. Alive, he is a symbol.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: A government that fears the Will of D. more than anything can't ignore a symbol.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So the Marines hunt Ace harder than they ever did before, and a hunted Ace is dangerous to them.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And his bounty can only go up from here.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Now, one man in canon is the reason the war ends: Shanks.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He arrives at the end, forces both sides to stop, and delivers a message that closes the war.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: In this version, he arrives the same way. But look at who is waiting.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: He sees Ace alive. He gives the Marines the same warning, and Ace hears it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: It's a small moment, but Shanks and Ace are not strangers. Shanks is the man who gave Luffy the straw hat.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Everyone in Ace's life, in this version, has a second chance to say something that never got said.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Whitebeard Pirates lose their father, but they keep their brother.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Marco, the first division commander, finally has someone to follow.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And that creates a new problem. Ace becomes the man the old crew rallies behind.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: A fire-user who is also a Roger and a former commander of the largest crew in the world.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That's a captain, and an Emperor in the making.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So what does the New World look like two years later?

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Luffy returns to Sabaody, reunites with his crew, and sails to Fish-Man Island. That part is set in stone.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace, meanwhile, has a rematch to fight. Blackbeard has two Devil Fruits and an army.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Teach is the man who took Thatch, took Whitebeard's power, and handed Ace to the Marines.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: This is a fight every fan wants, and it's the one canon took away.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Here's how it plays out, by the rules. Teach's Yami Yami no Mi nullifies Devil Fruit powers on contact.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace's flames will not work. He needs something else. Haki, strategy, and numbers.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That's where the Whitebeard Pirates come in. They aren't leaderless anymore.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: A campaign against Blackbeard, led by Ace, with Marco at his side.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And there's the point. Ace's survival doesn't remove the dark chapter. It moves it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Because Blackbeard doesn't need to fear Luffy first. He needs to fear Ace.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: That changes how he treats Luffy. Teach has to pick his fights.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: It also changes the final war. The Straw Hats don't have to be the only ones who stand against Teach.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: There is also a darker reading. If Ace lives, Luffy loses one of his clearest reasons to protect everyone.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And the Straw Hats would be the first to feel it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Because a captain with no graves to visit can still lose the people who sail beside him.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: So does Ace's survival make the world better? I'm not sure it does.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: It saves one brother and quietly breaks the other two's story.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Sabo never finds his memory in time. Luffy never meets him on the Dressrosa stage.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Luffy never learns what it means to carry someone's will, and that matters for who he becomes.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Here's my read: the death was cruel, but it was load-bearing.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Oda built the next twelve years of story on it. Sabo, the fruit, the vow, Whitebeard's legacy.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Pull it out, and the story survives. But it's a very different story.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Ace alive is a miracle. But a miracle in One Piece always comes with a bill, and Sabo is the one holding it.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: Which one would you rather have? Ace alive and Sabo lost, or the story as it is? Tell me which side you're on.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text

lines.text: And if you want to see what happens if Luffy had Gear 5 at Marineford, that's the next story.

shot.fallback: anime style pirate scene, dramatic lighting, no text
